deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is page 17 of the 1983 notes building the 'Teichmüller tower' as a category or groupoid S_A T^±_typ. Its objects are compact oriented (or ±) surfaces X with:
- a set A of circles C_a, split into cutting circles A_0 and free boundary circles A_ℓ;
- a structure R that attaches to each circle a 'repère'. The repère is a torsor R_a under a cyclic group Z_a/r_aZ_a, where Z_a ≅ π1(C_a) ≅ Z.

The combinatorial shadow is a bi-weighted graph. Vertices are the connected pieces, weighted by genus. Edges are the circles, weighted by r_a. Geometrically, a Z/r-torsor of repères on a circle is a set of r equally spaced marks (tangential basepoints) modulo rotation by 2π/r, or equivalently a μ_r-orbifold-type rigidification. The case r_a = 0 means the marking has been erased. The previous page has just described gluing two free boundary circles with equal weights r via the contracted product R_a ∧_{Z/r} R_a'.

This page lists the 'elementary operations' that should generate all morphisms or correspondences of the tower:
- 0°) Total direct sum, i.e. disjoint union of marked surfaces.
- 1°) Gommage (erasing) of the repères on gluing circles. On diagrams this is replacing some r_a by 0. The margin says it is irreversible.
- 2°) Restriction (reduction of structure group) from Z/r_a to its subgroup of order r'_a, where r'_a | r_a and d_a = r_a/r'_a > 1. Choosing r'_a equally spaced marks among r_a gives exactly d_a choices, as he notes. The margin calls this a strengthening of structure.
- 3°) Extension of structure group along Z/r_a ↪ Z/d_a r_a (multiplication by d_a): equally subdivide the marks. This is canonical, a weakening of structure, and inverse to 2° up to the d_a-fold choice. The crossed-out alternative name was 'gommage partiel/uniforme d'exposant d_a'.
- 4°) Erasing a cutting circle C_a (a ∈ A_0). In the graph this contracts an edge and merges two pieces.
- 5°) 'Bouchage' (capping) of the holes C_a (a ∈ A_ℓ): fill a boundary circle by a disc, (g,ν) → (g,ν−1).
- 6°) 'Découpage' (cutting open) along C_a (a ∈ A_0), producing two free boundary circles. A footnote suggests splitting 6° into the cases r_a = 0 and r_a ≠ 0, or excluding r_a = 0. Without a marking, the cut loses the twist information needed to reglue canonically.
- 7°) Gluing along two distinct free circles C_a, C_a' with r_a = r_a'. The gluing datum is an element of R_a ∧ R_a', i.e. one of r twist-matchings.

The margins classify which operations are (strongly) irreversible. 1° is irreversible when r_a ≠ 0. 6°/7° are irreversible if r_a = 0 and reversible (mutually inverse up to the torsor choice) if r_a ≠ 0.

The next page states a planned 'dévissage' theorem. Up to equivalence, the whole tower plus operations 1°–5° can be reconstructed from the connected one-vertex pieces S_1T^±_{g,ν} → T^±_{g,ν} → Ens(ν)×[±1], with all boundary weights 1. So the page is a generators-of-the-tower bookkeeping step in his Teichmüller-tower ('Lego') program.
errors: No outright mathematical error. A few looseness points:

The case r_a = 0 is used inconsistently. 'Z_a/0·Z_a = Z_a' would be the strongest structure, a Z-torsor, yet gommage 'replaces r_a by 0' as the absence of structure. Grothendieck himself flags the r_a = 0 case of 6° as problematic in his footnote.

Restriction (2°) is a correspondence (d_a choices), not a functor, whereas 3° is functorial. The list mixes functors and correspondences without saying so explicitly; the reversible/irreversible margins partially address this.

ideas.what: Category of surfaces with cutting/boundary circles carrying cyclic-torsor markings, with a list of elementary operations (disjoint union, erase marking, change marking order, erase cut, cap hole, cut, glue) generating the tower
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller 'Lego' / modular-operad structure on moduli of bordered surfaces with boundary parametrizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) for the Lego idea; formalized by Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (Lego-Teichmüller game, 2000), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §§2–3 (Teichmüller tower, 'jeu de Lego-Teichmüller'), only in outline

ideas.what: Gluing two boundary circles only when the cyclic weights agree (r_a = r_a'), with gluing data a point of the contracted product R_a ∧_{Z/r} R_a'
ideas.modern_name: Balanced nodes of twisted curves; clutching data as a μ_r-torsor of identifications / ghost automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abramovich–Vistoli (2002), Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli (2003), Olsson; in the topological setting, framed/marked gluing of Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov (1995)

ideas.what: Changing the order of the cyclic marking: reduction of structure group to an order-r' subgroup (d choices) vs. extension of structure group (canonical subdivision)
ideas.modern_name: Change of root/level structure on boundary markings (forgetful and refinement maps between r-marked moduli)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; appears in twisted-curve and r-spin literature (Chiodo, Jarvis)

ideas.what: Classification of the elementary operations into reversible and irreversible according to whether r_a = 0
ideas.modern_name: Distinction between invertible gluing (with parametrization) and lossy operations in modular-operad / Lego presentations

ideas.what: Planned dévissage (next page): the tower with its operations is determined by the one-vertex pieces S_1T^±_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of a modular operad from its corollas / generators and relations of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse) in the stronger low-modular-dimension form; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Getzler–Kapranov
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme states a stronger (dimension ≤2) version

missed.claim: Grothendieck's tower uses boundary circles weighted by cyclic orders r_a, with Z/r_a-torsors of repères. Gluing is only allowed for equal weights, via the contracted product of the torsors, and the order can be changed by reduction or extension of the cyclic structure group. This is essentially the topological/combinatorial shadow of twisted (orbifold) stable curves with balanced nodes and μ_r gluing data, formalized two decades later. The link between the Lego tower and twisted-curve stacks (orbifold M_{g,n} with μ_r at markings and nodes) is not usually attributed to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: 7°) Recollement le long de C_a, C_{a'} (a, a' ∈ A_ℓ, a ≠ a', r_a = r_{a'}), via un élément de R_a ∧ R_{a'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a Galois-Teichmüller tower built from twisted-curve stacks with all r-levels, together with level-changing maps 2°/3°. This is a natural setting for extending GT-actions to stacks of twisted or r-spin curves, but it is only sporadically explored.

missed.claim: The case r_a = 0 (unmarked circles) under cutting is left undecided: split operation 6°, or exclude r_a = 0? The dévissage theorem on the following page is only announced, not proved.
missed.quote: Il faudrait peut-être séparer 6°) en deux, suivant que r_a = 0 ou r_a ≠ 0 (ou exclure le cas r_a = 0 ?)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Modern presentations (Bakalov–Kirillov, HLS) resolve this by always parametrizing boundaries, so the gap is essentially filled by later work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but mostly bookkeeping list of generating operations for the Teichmüller Lego, consistent with the Esquisse. The mildly notable detail is the systematic use of cyclic weights r_a with torsor gluing and reduction/extension of structure group. That anticipates the balanced-node formalism of twisted curves, but it is sketchy and largely recovered by later Lego and modular-operad literature.
transcription_corrections: 5°) 'bordage des trous' is more likely 'bouchage des trous' (capping holes), which fits a ∈ A_ℓ.
6°) 'Dilatages le long de C_a' is more likely 'Découpages le long de C_a' (cutting along cutting circles a ∈ A_0), the natural inverse of 7°.
Margin by 2°: 'transformations structures fortes' is likely 'renforcements de structures' (reduction of structure group). The margin by 3° reads 'affaiblissements de structures'.
Margins 'fortunes irréversibles' are likely 'fortement irréversibles' or similar; the bottom margin reads roughly 'Fortement irréversibles 6°) si r_a = 0, réversibles si r_a ≠ ...'.
Line 1: 'Somme directe totale, de repères' with a cross-out. The repères are said to lie 'sur des cercles de recollement'.
Margin by 2°: 'r'_a ≠ r_a i.e. d_a = r_a/r'_a ≠ 1' (the duplicated 'r'_a ≠ r_a et r'_a ≠ r_a' is a transcription artifact).
